cases.sentence: Дарья Александровна с своей стороны была в этот день в ___.
cases.explain: «большом огорчении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: After escorting his wife upstairs, Levin went to Dolly’s part of the house. Darya Alexandrovna, for her part, was in great distress too that day. She was walking about the room, talking angrily to a little girl, who stood in the corner roaring.

cases.sentence: – Нет, это ___! – обратилась она к Левину. – Откуда берутся у нее эти мерзкие наклонности?
cases.explain: «гадкая девочка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Oh, she is a disgusting child!” she turned to Levin. “Where does she get such wicked propensities?”

cases.sentence: – Нет, это гадкая девочка! – обратилась она к Левину. – Откуда берутся у нее эти ___?
cases.explain: «мерзкие наклонности» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Oh, she is a disgusting child!” she turned to Levin. “Where does she get such wicked propensities?”

cases.sentence: – Это ничего не доказывает, это совсем не ___, это просто шалость, – успокоивал ее Левин.
cases.explain: «гадкие наклонности» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “That proves nothing; it’s not a question of evil propensities at all, it’s simply mischief,” Levin assured her.

cases.sentence: Мы поссорились ___ с тех пор, как…
cases.explain: «второй раз» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “I’ve not been in there, I’ve been alone in the garden with Kitty. We’ve had a quarrel for the second time since … Stiva came.”

cases.sentence: Левин застал Васеньку в то время, как тот, разобрав свои вещи из чемодана и разложив ___, примеривал краги, чтоб ездить верхом.
cases.explain: «новые романсы» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Levin came upon Veslovsky at the moment when the latter, having unpacked his things from his trunk, and laid out some new songs, was putting on his gaiters to go out riding.

cases.sentence: – Да, это гораздо чище, – сказал Васенька, ставя жирную ногу на стул, застегивая ___ и весело, добродушно улыбаясь.
cases.explain: «нижний крючок» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Yes, it’s much cleaner,” said Vassenka, putting his fat leg on a chair, fastening the bottom hook, and smiling with simple-hearted good humor.

cases.sentence: – Случилось, что я жду гостей, – сказал Левин, быстрее и быстрее обламывая ___ концы расщепившейся палки. – И не жду гостей, и ничего не случилось, но я прошу вас уехать.
cases.explain: «сильными пальцами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “It happens that I expect visitors,” said Levin, his strong fingers more and more rapidly breaking off the ends of the split stick. “And I’m not expecting visitors, and nothing has happened, but I beg you to go away. You can explain my rudeness as you like.”

cases.sentence: И так как расщепившиеся концы были уже все отломаны, Левин зацепился пальцами за ___, разодрал палку и старательно поймал падавший конец.
cases.explain: «толстые концы» — after the preposition «за», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: And as the split ends were all broken off, Levin clutched the thick ends in his finger, broke the stick in two, and carefully caught the end as it fell.

cases.sentence: Вероятно, вид этих напряженных рук, тех ___, которые он нынче утром ощупывал на гимнастике, и блестящих глаз, тихого голоса и дрожащих скул убедили Васеньку больше слов.
cases.explain: «самых мускулов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Probably the sight of those nervous fingers, of the muscles he had proved that morning at gymnastics, of the glittering eyes, the soft voice, and quivering jaws, convinced Vassenka better than any words. He bowed, shrugging his shoulders, and smiling contemptuously.

cases.sentence: Вероятно, вид этих напряженных рук, тех самых мускулов, которые он нынче утром ощупывал на гимнастике, и ___, тихого голоса и дрожащих скул убедили Васеньку больше слов.
cases.explain: «блестящих глаз» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Probably the sight of those nervous fingers, of the muscles he had proved that morning at gymnastics, of the glittering eyes, the soft voice, and quivering jaws, convinced Vassenka better than any words. He bowed, shrugging his shoulders, and smiling contemptuously.

cases.sentence: Вероятно, вид этих напряженных рук, тех самых мускулов, которые он нынче утром ощупывал на гимнастике, и блестящих глаз, ___ и дрожащих скул убедили Васеньку больше слов.
cases.explain: «тихого голоса» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Probably the sight of those nervous fingers, of the muscles he had proved that morning at gymnastics, of the glittering eyes, the soft voice, and quivering jaws, convinced Vassenka better than any words. He bowed, shrugging his shoulders, and smiling contemptuously.

cases.explain: «молодой человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “What madness is this?” Stepan Arkadyevitch said when, after hearing from his friend that he was being turned out of the house, he found Levin in the garden, where he was walking about waiting for his guest’s departure. “Mais c’est ridicule! What fly has stung you? Mais c’est du dernier ridicule! What did you think, if a young man. …”

cases.sentence: Скоро он услыхал грохот тарантаса и увидал из-за деревьев, как Васенька, сидя на сене (на беду не было сиденья в тарантасе) в своей ___, подпрыгивая по толчкам, проехал по аллее.
cases.explain: «шотландской шапочке» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Levin turned quickly, and walked away from him into the depths of the avenue, and he went on walking up and down alone. Soon he heard the rumble of the trap, and saw from behind the trees how Vassenka, sitting in the hay (unluckily there was no seat in the trap) in his Scotch cap, was driven along the avenue, jolting up and down over the ruts.
